title: Power Transmission & Belt Drives — Theory
subtitle: Belt drives are one of the most common ways to transmit power — they're on bicycles, washing machines, car engines. This week covers the theory: open vs cross belts, slip, creep, angle of contact, velocity ratio, and the all-important tension ratio.
learningOutcome: Belt drives are one of the most common ways to transmit power — they're on bicycles, washing machines, car engines. This week covers the theory: open vs cross belts, slip, creep, angle of contact, velocity ratio, and the all-important tension ratio.

content.text:
Exam-ready definition (from notes):
Power transmission is used to transfer power from the prime mover to the moving machine [source to driven machine]. A transmission system is the combination of clutch and gearbox. It is a mechanical device which varies the engine torque according to the driver requirement.

items: Open belt system: pulleys rotate in the SAME direction
Cross belt system: pulleys rotate in OPPOSITE directions (belt crosses itself)
Creep: extension of belt on tight side and contraction at slack side
Slip: relative motion between pulley and belt, expressed as percentage (ε = 0.01 to 0.03)

content.text: N_s = speed of smaller pulley (rpm) · N_L = speed of larger pulley · D_L = diameter of large pulley · D_s = diameter of small pulley · S₁, S₂ = slip percentages
C = centre-to-centre distance · β = angle of lap · Use smaller θ in tension ratio formula
T₁ = tension in tight side · T₂ = tension in slack side · Tc = centrifugal tension · μ = coefficient of friction · θ = angle of contact (radians)
C = centre distance (m) · D_L, D_s = pulley diameters (m)

content.caption: Open belt vs cross belt — angle of contact
content.description: OPEN BELT · Same direction rotation · Driver · Driven · CROSS BELT · Opposite direction rotation

content.text: Common mistake — Using the LARGE pulley's angle of contact in the tension ratio. Always use the SMALLER angle (which is on the smaller pulley for open belts). The belt slips first where the wrap angle is smallest. Using the wrong θ gives a completely wrong tension ratio.

items: • Define power transmission. State the types of belt drives.
• Derive/state the tension ratio T₁/T₂ = e^(μθ). Know what each symbol means.
• Calculate velocity ratio including slip. Know the difference between open and cross belt angle of contact formulas.
